best_lineage.idea: Replace the O(n log n) merge sort with an O(n) LSD radix sort using 4 passes of 8 bits each, with integrated skip-detection (skip a pass when all keys share that digit) and insertion-sort fallback for small n, which should dramatically speed up uniform and nearly-sorted distributions while matching std::sort on all inputs.

Add a direct counting-sort branch for inputs whose maximum value is below 1000 (the many-duplicate distribution), replacing the 4-pass radix path for that case; this leaves the full-range radix unchanged and gives a large speedup on that distribution, raising the geometric mean.

Sweep the radix sort's bits-per-pass and number-of-passes parameters to find the fastest configuration covering the full 32-bit range, alongside sweeping the counting-sort bucket count and insertion-sort threshold.
